# RigorRun

> Acceptance testing for AI agents that take real actions. A person demonstrates
> a real job once; RigorRun derives the rules from what changed in the system,
> generates an executable acceptance suite, runs an agent against it, and decides
> pass or fail by reading the system state afterwards rather than the agent's own
> account of what it did.

RigorRun is a local-first CLI and web interface, published on npm as `rigorrun`,
MIT licensed, with SLSA build provenance. It runs entirely on the user's machine:
there is no account and no hosted component.

## Key distinctions

- It is not an LLM evaluation harness. Evals score a model's output text.
  RigorRun compares system state before and after, through read operations the
  operator nominates.
- Every verdict carries a verification strength: AUTHORITATIVE, PARTIAL or
  OBSERVATIONAL. A verdict against a real external system is PARTIAL by design.
- A browser-only connection is OBSERVATIONAL: the DOM is not authoritative state.
- Isolation is reported as RESET, PARTIAL, DECLARED or NONE. DECLARED means a
  reset was nominated but never observed to work.

## Docs

- Getting started: https://rigorrun.xyz/start

- Evidence, against MCP servers written by others: https://rigorrun.xyz/evidence

- Full documentation: https://docs.rigorrun.xyz

## Honest limits

No external team has used RigorRun yet. There are no customers, no funding and no
revenue. Published evidence covers four MCP servers from a single publisher, in
which 19 of 37 tools were exercised; the remainder are itemised with reasons.
